Alice — great questions. Short answers up front, then details.

TL;DR:
- Redwood supports both 1536 and 768 embedding dims depending on model choice; we can preserve 1536 for parity and run experiments on 768 for cost tradeoffs.
- We recommend L2-normalization when using cosine similarity; Redwood offers an automatic normalization flag at ingest time so you can keep your current downstream logic intact.
- Backfill batching: we typically recommend 64-256 embeddings per request for stable throughput; for bulk ingestion we have a backfill tool that streams into the embed ingestion pipeline in parallel (we can share the script).
- Auth: for hosted API, scoped API keys are standard; mTLS/service-account keys are available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Details:
1) Dimensions and model parity
- If you want drop-in parity with minimal downstream changes, keep 1536. If cost is a bigger lever, we can run A/B tests with a 768-d variant and measure quality on your evaluation set.
- We can produce a parity report showing nearest-neighbor overlap and MAP@k.

2) Normalization
- L2-normalization + cosine is the most common pattern. Redwood's embed endpoint can return already-normalized vectors (set normalize=true). If you prefer storing raw vectors, we recommend normalizing at query time for consistency.

3) Batching and throughput
- For small documents where each embedding is short, we recommend batching 128-512 records per embed call. Larger docs or long contexts reduce batch size for latency reasons.
- For bulk backfill we use parallel workers and recommend chunk sizes of ~1k rows per worker with each worker sending smaller batches to the embed endpoint (e.g., 128). This keeps GPU memory utilization steady and reduces OOM risk.
- We'll provide a sample backfill script and a perf table for 1536 vs 768 dims.

4) Migration pattern
- Dual-write for 7-14 days (your writes go to both providers)
- Run parity checks daily and hold traffic on Redwood for a subset of traffic (canary)
- Backfill historical index with our bulk ingestion tool; we can provide a backfill runbook and sample scripts.

I attached a short checklist in the migration plan. Happy to run a parity pass on your sample — attaching a link to the checklist and our backfill script in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_migration_assets

Thanks — looping Dev to cover SDK/auth details.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — Dev from Solutions Engineering here. A few concrete notes to help your engineers get started: 

SDK setup (example flows)
- Our SDKs (Python/Node/Go) have a single Embeddings client: EmbedClient(api_key="REDACTED").create_embeddings(items=[]) or embed_client.batch_create(items, batch_size=128).
- We also expose a bulk ingestion CLI tool (redwood backfill --input csv --parallel 8 --batch-size 128) that handles retry, rate limiting, and checkpointing for resumed runs.

Auth options
- Hosted: scoped API keys with role-based scopes (recommended for initial migration). Keys can be created in Console and rotated.
- Dedicated/Private: we support mTLS and service-account keys (long-lived credentials bound to a project). If you need HSM/KMS integration, we can coordinate with your security team.

Routing and reranker tips
- Use separate endpoints for: /v1/embeddings (for vector creation) and /v1/rerank (if you use a supervised reranker). You can route requests at the SDK layer using a customer-configurable policy: prefer local reranker for latency-sensitive flows, fall back to hosted reranker for cost/coverage.
- For structured output / tool calling: if you plan to use function/tool calling for downstream re-ranking or metadata extraction, keep the embedding generation synchronous and then call the tool with top-k candidates.

Auth example (Python):
# pseudocode
from redwood import EmbedClient
client = EmbedClient(api_key="YOUR_SCOPED_KEY")
# batch helper handles chunking and retry
client.batch_create(items, batch_size=128)

We can share a runnable example repo. If you want, we can spin up a short working session with your eng team to get the SDK keys and a test backfill running.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
